summary.short: Rules under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, published 13 November 2025, set how Data Fiduciaries must give notices, secure data, notify breaches, erase data and obtain verifiable parental consent. They also cover Consent Manager registration, Significant Data Fiduciary duties, State processing standards and Data Protection Board procedure, with staged commencement.
summary.long: Rules made under sections 40(1) and 40(2) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, published in the Gazette of India on 13 November 2025. Rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21 apply from publication; Rule 4 (Consent Managers) applies one year after publication; Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 apply eighteen months after publication. Rule 3 sets content requirements for notices to Data Principals. Rule 4 and the First Schedule provide for Board registration of Consent Managers and their obligations. Rule 5 and the Second Schedule set standards for State processing for subsidies, benefits, licences and permits. Rule 6 requires reasonable security safeguards; Rule 7 requires breach notices to Data Principals and to the Board within seventy-two hours. Rule 8 and the Third Schedule set erasure periods for listed e-commerce, online gaming and social media intermediaries. Rules 10 and 11 require verifiable consent for children and guardian verification for persons with disability; Rule 12 and the Fourth Schedule list exempt classes. Rule 13 imposes periodic impact assessment and audit on Significant Data Fiduciaries and restricts transfer of specified data outside India. Rule 14 sets rights-request procedures and a ninety-day grievance period. Rule 15 allows transfers abroad subject to government requirements; Rule 16 exempts research, archiving and statistical processing. Rules 17 to 23 cover Board appointments, meetings, digital proceedings, appeals to the Appellate Tribunal and government information requests. The rules themselves state no penalty amounts.

notes: Rules made under section 40(1) and (2) of the Act; the Act is not part of this text, so target_instrument_id is blank in all relations and the Act is named in target_text. Commencement is staggered: rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21 apply from publication, rule 4 one year after, and rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 eighteen months after (rule 1(2) to (4)). Internal inconsistency: rule 13(5) names the 'Ministry of Electronics and Technology', while rule 17 and the Seventh Schedule name the 'Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology'. The Hindi and English texts are both official in the gazette; quotes are from the English text. The draft published on 3 January 2025 (G.S.R. 02(E)) is mentioned in the preamble and is not annotated here.
